rules.build: # PAM_CAP: the makefile only builds the module when it finds the header of # PAM in /usr/include, which is not where the tools folder has it. # FORCELINKPAM: link pam_cap.so with libpam, as Debian does. cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make \ prefix="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" \ lib=lib \ CROSS_COMPILE="${AELTRA_HOST_TYPE}-" \ DYNAMIC=yes \ FORCELINKPAM=yes \ GOLANG=no \ PAM_CAP=yes \ -j"$AELTRA_PARALLEL_JOBS"
rules.install:
cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make \ DESTDIR="$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR" \ prefix="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" \ lib=lib \ PKGCONFIGDIR="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig" \ CROSS_COMPILE="${AELTRA_HOST_TYPE}-" \ DYNAMIC=yes \ FORCELINKPAM=yes \ GOLANG=no \ PAM_CAP=yes \ RAISE_SETFCAP=no \ install
install -d -m 0755 "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/security" install -m 644 pam_cap/capability.conf "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/security/"
install -d -m 0755 \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/share/pam-configs" install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/pam-configs/capability" \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/share/pam-configs/"
